solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: QC who might get you a beer?

definitions.meaning: a Queen's Counsel is a senior barrister, a member of the Bar

definitions.text: who might get you a beer?
definitions.meaning: someone serving behind a pub counter

explanation.surface: A puzzle about which helpful person fetches you a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as BAR MAN, the word describes a lawyer called to the Bar; read whole, it is the pub worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrister belongs to the Bar, and a pub server works behind the bar, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Important film about American offender

indicators.note: the important film goes around the American abbreviation, which sits in the middle

parts.note: big means important
a mist is a thin film or haze

explanation.surface: A major movie concerning a US criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' is not a movie here but a thin haze; the container splits the phrase between its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Marrying while already married is a crime, so such a person breaks the law.

clue.text: Unexpected merits of Republican, one wanting change

indicators.note: unexpected means out of the ordinary order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The surprising virtues of a US Republican politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A campaigner for gradual political or social improvement wants things altered.

clue.text: Frightened of nothing, back on attack

indicators.note: back means the letters for nothing are read in the reverse direction

parts.note: FA, short for sweet FA, is British slang for nothing at all
a raid is a sudden attack

explanation.surface: Scared of nothing, someone returns to the offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweet FA is British slang for nothing at all; 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Scared, fearful and alarmed all describe someone in a state of fear.

clue.text: Make prettier grooming instrument in Bow

indicators.note: Bow is in London's East End, where a Cockney accent drops the opening h of a word

parts.note: a tool for tidying the hair on your head

explanation.surface: Someone smartens up with a comb or brush while in an East London district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Bow' asks for the word as a Cockney would say it, dropping the H. Bow is a district of East London, home of the Cockney.
explanation.definitionFit: To retouch a photo with a fine spray tool is to make it look better than reality.

clue.text: Rash of sensible prior to go walkabout

indicators.note: to wander off aimlessly, so the letters stray into a new order

explanation.surface: A sensible person's reckless decision to wander off, Australian style.
explanation.definitionFit: Hasty and reckless, acting without due care, is a common sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Get fat fool to support reactionary party

indicators.note: in a down clue the fool sits below the party, holding it up
reacting against, moving backwards, so the party's letters are read in reverse

parts.note: Lab is short for Labour, a UK political party
a loon is a silly, crazy person

explanation.surface: An idiot backing a right-wing party, which then puts on weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reactionary' suggests the political right, but here signals a turnaround of Labour's short form.
explanation.definitionFit: To swell or expand rapidly, as someone's weight does, is to swell up.

clue.text: Complete madman losing head

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for madman is dropped

parts.note: nutter is British slang for a crazy person

explanation.surface: A total lunatic who has lost his mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Total, absolute, as in an absolute disaster: an adjective of degree.

clue.text: Intruder with a very bad cough?

definitions.meaning: someone who breaks into computer systems
a person who keeps coughing harshly

explanation.surface: A burglar betrayed by his terrible cough.
explanation.definitionFit: Computer criminals break into networks; to hack is also to cough harshly and repeatedly.

clue.text: Succeed in attempt to join rebellious force

parts.note: have a go means make an attempt

indicators.note: a rebel turns against things, so the letters for force are turned round

parts.note: the RAF is the Royal Air Force

explanation.surface: Advice to make a bid at signing up with a mutinous army.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who will go far is expected to do well in life: an idiom for success.

clue.text: A typical Romeo, dishevelled and completely drunk

indicators.note: untidy, messed up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An ordinary lover, rumpled and very much the worse for drink.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for extremely intoxicated, from the sense of being unable to move.

clue.text: Boozer who'll succeed one day?

definitions.meaning: British slang for a pub, many of which take royal names
the heir apparent to the British throne

explanation.surface: A drunk who expects to do well eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boozer' suggests a drinker; it is British slang for a pub, and this is a common pub name.
explanation.definitionFit: The title given to the British monarch's heir, and a familiar name for a pub.

clue.text: Cocktail dress inspiring a riot on vacation

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the dress takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: a mini is a short dress

indicators.note: vacated, emptied of its middle, leaving only the outside letters of riot

explanation.surface: A cocktail dress that provokes a riot when its wearer goes on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' means emptied of its inner letters; 'Cocktail dress' looks like one phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin and vermouth mixed drink is a classic example of a cocktail.

clue.text: Psycho regularly has longing to torment

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, here every second one of Psycho

parts.note: an urge is a strong desire

explanation.surface: A disturbed killer often feels a desire to inflict suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: To whip or afflict severely, so to cause great suffering, as a verb.

clue.text: What you might do after knocking back lager?

definitions.text: What you might do after knocking back lager?

parts.words: What you might do after knocking back lager?
parts.note: after downing too much beer your head goes round and round

explanation.surface: A question about the effects of drinking beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking back' hints at reading backwards, but no letters are turned; it simply means drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Drinking too much leaves the room whirling, so you feel dizzy and whirl yourself.

clue.text: Ship carrying amontillado perhaps

definitions.meaning: a sailing vessel with fore-and-aft rigged masts
a tall sherry glass, amontillado being a type of sherry

explanation.surface: A vessel transporting a cargo of sherry.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a two-masted sailing vessel and a large glass used for sherry or beer.

clue.text: Performance that's sometimes extraordinary

definitions.meaning: a rendering of a song or play
extraordinary ... is the transfer of suspects to another country for interrogation

explanation.surface: A show that is occasionally remarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: A performance is an interpretation of a piece of music, and the word pairs with extraordinary in the political phrase.

clue.text: Row about Spice Girl's frilly knickers?

indicators.note: around, so the row encloses the Spice Girl

parts.note: a line is a row
Geri Halliwell was Ginger Spice in the Spice Girls; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: A quarrel over a pop star's underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spice Girls were a 1990s British pop group; Geri was one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Women's underwear and nightclothes, of which lacy knickers are an example.

clue.text: Winner in race to reform Tories

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A political slogan: the winning path is to remake the Conservative party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' rearranges TORIES to RTOISE, after TO. Tories are Britain's Conservatives.
explanation.definitionFit: In Aesop's fable the slow reptile beats the hare in their contest.

clue.text: Reticence of penniless guard

indicators.note: without a penny, and P is the abbreviation for penny, so that letter goes

parts.note: to preserve is to protect or guard

explanation.surface: The quietness of a broke security guard.
explanation.definitionFit: Restraint and reluctance to show feelings, keeping oneself back.

clue.text: Hostile to some arrogant incumbents

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Opposed to certain haughty office-holders.
explanation.definitionFit: Being against something or someone means being opposed and unfriendly to it.

clue.text: Virgin reported being pursued

indicators.note: reported speech is heard, so the word for virgin is spoken and its sound written down

parts.note: someone chaste is sexually pure, like a virgin

explanation.surface: A newspaper story about a virgin being followed.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunted or followed in pursuit, as a past participle meaning run after.

clue.text: Duke unpleasant about German skivvy

indicators.note: around, so the unpleasant word wraps the German

parts.note: rude means unpleasant or offensive

explanation.surface: An aristocrat being nasty to his German servant.
explanation.walkthrough: Skivvy is British slang for a lowly domestic servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A menial worker doing hard boring tasks is a lowly servant.

clue.text: One cutting journo's expression of disapproval

parts.note: a hack is a journalist, and the 's here reads as 'is'
aw is an exclamation of protest or dismay

explanation.surface: A journalist's tut-tut at someone cutting copy.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal-cutting tool with a fine-toothed blade is something that cuts.

clue.text: Tax evader failing to finish well-fed fowl

indicators.note: the last letter of the gangster's name is not reached

parts.note: Al Capone, the Chicago gangster, was jailed for tax evasion

explanation.surface: A tax dodger who fails to finish his rich meal of chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: A castrated cockerel fattened for the table is a plump bird.

clue.text: Cuckoo behaving like a dog?

definitions.meaning: making the sound a dog makes, woofing

explanation.surface: A bird that acts like a hound.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for mad (as in barking mad), and literally yelping as a dog does.

clue.text: I will make a quite outstanding Bond

definitions.text: I will make a quite outstanding Bond

parts.words: I will make a quite outstanding Bond
parts.note: a bond is an adhesive join, and the product boasts of an excellent one

explanation.surface: An actor's boast of becoming a superb James Bond.
explanation.walkthrough: Bond is capitalised to suggest 007, but here it is a join made by adhesive.
explanation.definitionFit: A very strong quick-setting adhesive makes an excellent join between surfaces.

clue.text: Flatter doctor I placed beside queen

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A medic flatters the monarch by setting himself next to her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flatter' looks like a verb meaning praise; it is the comparative, more flat or dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Duller, less lively, as in a more arid or boring style: both mean comparatively lacking sparkle.

clue.text: Exotic Sudanese artiste

indicators.note: something exotic is unusual and foreign, so these letters take on an unfamiliar arrangement

explanation.surface: A foreign performer from Sudan.
explanation.definitionFit: A female ballet dancer is a performer on stage, an artiste.

clue.text: Yours truly, occasionally jaundiced and a bit of a Scrooge

parts.note: the writer's way of saying me

indicators.note: only now and then, so every second letter of jaundiced is taken

explanation.surface: The writer admits to being somewhat bitter and rather stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: A stingy, ungenerous person, like Dickens's miser Ebenezer Scrooge.
